187: func generatePlugin() string {
188: 	return `import type {
189:   AgentEndEvent,
190:   AgentStartEvent,
191:   PluginAPI,
192:   SessionStartEvent,
193:   ThreadMessage,
194: } from "@ampcode/plugin";
195: import { execFile } from "node:child_process";

197: // entire-agent-amp: project-local Entire integration for Amp.
198: export default function (amp: PluginAPI) {
199:   // In-memory session tracking.
200:   let currentThreadId: string | null = null;
201:   const seenThreads = new Set<string>();
202: 
203:   // trackThread records the given thread id and returns true when it is the
204:   // first time we have seen it for the current session. When a different
205:   // thread id is discovered we clear all tracking — the user has switched to
206:   // a new thread, so prior dedupe state no longer applies.
207:   function trackThread(threadId: string): boolean {
208:     if (threadId !== currentThreadId) {
209:       seenThreads.clear();
210:       currentThreadId = threadId;
211:     }
212:     if (seenThreads.has(threadId)) return false;
213:     seenThreads.add(threadId);
214:     return true;
215:   }
216: 
217:   function fireHook(hookName: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
218:     return new Promise((resolve) => {
219:       let body: string;
220:       try {
221:         body = JSON.stringify(data);
222:       } catch (err) {
223:         amp.logger.log("entire hook stringify failed", hookName, err);
224:         resolve();
225:         return;
226:       }
227: 
228:       // NOTE: we await this from request handlers (agent.start/agent.end) on
229:       // purpose — Entire's transcript ordering depends on hooks completing in
230:       // sequence. Do not convert to fire-and-forget.
231:       const child = execFile(
232:         "entire",
233:         ["hooks", "amp", hookName],
234:         { timeout: 10_000, windowsHide: true, maxBuffer: Infinity },
235:         (err, _stdout, stderr) => {
236:           if (err) {
237:             amp.logger.log("entire hook failed", hookName, err.message, stderr);
238:           }
239:           resolve();
240:         },
241:       );
242:       child.stdin?.end(body);
243:     });
244:   }
245: 
246:   function modifiedFiles(messages: ThreadMessage[]): string[] {
247:     const files = new Set<string>();
248:     for (const item of amp.helpers.toolCallsInMessages(messages)) {
249:       for (const event of [item.call, item.result]) {
250:         const modified = amp.helpers.filesModifiedByToolCall(event);
251:         if (!modified) continue;
252:         for (const file of modified) files.add(amp.helpers.filePathFromURI(file));
253:       }
254:     }
255:     return Array.from(files).sort();
256:   }
257: 
258:   amp.on("session.start", async (event: SessionStartEvent): Promise<void> => {
259:     const threadId = event.thread?.id;
260:     if (!threadId) return;
261:     if (!trackThread(threadId)) return;
262:     await fireHook("session.start", {
263:       type: "session.start",
264:       cwd: process.cwd(),
265:       thread_id: threadId,
266:     });
267:   });
268: 
269:   amp.on("agent.start", async (event: AgentStartEvent): Promise<void> => {
270:     // Amp's session.start does not always include a thread id, so agent.start
271:     // is the fallback point for firing the synthetic session.start hook.
272:     if (trackThread(event.thread.id)) {
273:       await fireHook("session.start", {
274:         type: "session.start",
275:         cwd: process.cwd(),
276:         thread_id: event.thread.id,
277:       });
278:     }
279: 
280:     await fireHook("agent.start", {
281:       type: "agent.start",
282:       cwd: process.cwd(),
283:       thread_id: event.thread.id,
284:       message_id: String(event.id),
285:       message: event.message,
286:     });
287:   });
288: 
289:   amp.on("agent.end", async (event: AgentEndEvent): Promise<void> => {
290:     await fireHook("agent.end", {
291:       type: "agent.end",
292:       cwd: process.cwd(),
293:       thread_id: event.thread.id,
294:       message_id: String(event.id),
295:       message: event.message,
296:       status: event.status,
297:       messages: event.messages,
298:       modified_files: modifiedFiles(event.messages),
299:     });
300:   });
301: }

22: 	if strings.TrimSpace(threadID) == "" {
23: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("thread ID is required")
24: 	}
25: 	if strings.TrimSpace(outputPath) == "" {
26: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("output path is required")
27: 	}

29: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("create output dir: %w", err)
30: 	}
31:

33: 	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "PLUGINS=all")
34: 	out, err := cmd.Output()
35: 	if err != nil {

4:

21: - Plugin loading: run `PLUGINS=all amp ...`.
22: 
23: ## Hook Mechanism
24: - Config file: `.amp/plugins/entire.ts`
25: - Config format: TypeScript plugin running on Amp's Bun-provided runtime.
26: - Hook registration: plugin default export receives `PluginAPI`, registers handlers with `amp.on(event, handler)`.
27: - Hook names and protocol mapping:
28: 
29: | Native Hook Name | When It Fires | Protocol Event Type |
30: |------------------|---------------|---------------------|
31: | synthetic `session.start` | before first `agent.start` per thread | 1 = SessionStart |
32: | `agent.start` | user submits a prompt | 2 = TurnStart |
33: | `agent.end` | agent finishes a turn | 3 = TurnEnd |
34:

36:

38: - Session ID source: Amp `thread.id`.
39: - Session directory: `.entire/tmp/amp/`.
40: - Bootstrap session file format: JSONL hook cache written by the external agent binary from plugin payloads.
41: - Prepared session file format: exported Amp thread JSON, parsed as `AmpThread` from `internal/amp/types.go`.
42: - Resume mechanism: `PLUGINS=all amp threads continue <thread-id>`.
43:

45: - Bootstrap location: `.entire/tmp/amp/<safe-thread-id>.json` before preparation. The file contains JSONL hook entries with at least `type`, `thread_id`, and optional prompt text.
46: - Retrieval: `prepare-transcript --session-ref <path>` reads the bootstrap JSONL, extracts `thread_id`, runs `amp threads export <thread-id>`, and writes the exported JSON back to the same `session_ref` path.

48: - Authoritative parser: `internal/amp/types.go` models the exported transcript as `AmpThread`, `ThreadMessage`, `ThreadContentBlock`, `ThreadToolRun`, and `ThreadUsage`.
49: - User prompt extraction: `AmpThread.Messages[].Content[]` text blocks on `role: "user"` messages.
50: - Assistant summary extraction: last non-empty text block on `role: "assistant"` messages.
51: - Modified file extraction: `ThreadToolRun.TrackFiles`, tool input path fields (`path`, `filePath`, `filepath`, `file`, `absolutePath`, `paths`, `files`), and common tool result `absolutePath` fields.
52: - Token usage extraction: `ThreadMessage.Usage` on exported messages.
53: - Unprepared behavior: transcript analyzer, compact transcript, token calculation, and read-session operations require exported `AmpThread` JSON and return an error if called on the bootstrap JSONL cache before `prepare-transcript`.

# Plan: Remove bootstrap transcript; export on session.start and agent.end

## Goals
- Drop the JSONL "bootstrap" cache concept from `entire-agent-amp`. The exported Amp thread JSON is the sole source of truth.
- Trigger `amp threads export <thread-id>` from `ParseHook` only on `session.start` and `agent.end`. `agent.start` does not export (falls back to existing file; re-exports only if file is missing).
- Keep `PrepareTranscript` as a "refresh" operation that re-exports using the thread ID found inside the existing prepared transcript at `sessionRef`.

## Code changes

### `internal/amp/transcript.go`
- Delete the bootstrap-only API:
  - `ampTranscriptEntry` struct
  - `appendTranscriptEntry`
  - `readBootstrapEntries`
  - `bootstrapThreadID`
  - `newJSONLScanner` and `maxScannerLine` (only used by bootstrap reader)
- Rewrite `PrepareTranscript(sessionRef)`:
  - Read `sessionRef`.
  - Parse as `AmpThread` (existing `parseAmpThread`); error if the file is missing or not a prepared transcript.
  - Use `thread.ID` and call `runner.ExportThread(ctx, thread.ID, sessionRef)` to refresh.

### `internal/amp/hooks.go`
- Remove `appendBootstrapTranscriptEntry` (and all its call sites).
- Introduce a small helper, e.g. `(a *Agent) exportThread(threadID, sessionRef string) error`, that mkdirs `filepath.Dir(sessionRef)` and runs `ExportThread` with the existing `prepareTranscriptTimeout`. Errors are swallowed/returned consistently with current behavior (return empty model on failure, keep emitting the event).
- Refactor `ParseHook`:
  - `session.start`: call `exportThread(...)` (best effort), then read latest model from the prepared transcript, return Type 1 event.
  - `agent.start`: do **not** export by default. Read `sessionRef` and parse `AmpThread`; if missing/invalid, call `exportThread(...)` once as a fallback so the model can still be reported. Return Type 2 event with `Prompt = payload.Message`.
  - `agent.end`: call `exportThread(...)` to capture the freshly-completed turn; read latest model; return Type 3 event.
- `modelFromExportedThread` becomes either removed or simplified into `latestModelFromSessionRef(sessionRef string) string` that only reads the file (no export side-effect). All explicit exports happen in the hook switch.

### Tests

`internal/amp/hooks_test.go`
- Update `TestParseHookSessionStart`: still expects export (`assertExportedThread`).
- Update `TestParseHookAgentStartWritesTranscript`:
  - When no prepared file exists: assert agent.start triggers a fallback export (model = "claude").
  - Add a sibling test where a prepared file is pre-written: assert agent.start does NOT call `ExportThread` (runner unchanged) and still reports the model.
- Update `TestParseHookAgentEndWritesTranscript`: still expects export.
- Existing `TestParseHookUsesSessionRefExportedThreadModel` already covers "prepared file present → no re-export" for session.start; keep it.

`internal/amp/transcript_test.go`
- Replace `TestPrepareTranscript`: pre-write a prepared `AmpThread` JSON at `path`; call `PrepareTranscript`; assert runner saw `threadID == "T-123"` and `outputPath == path`; assert file contents are the runner-written JSON.
- Replace `TestPrepareTranscript_MissingThreadID` with `TestPrepareTranscript_UnpreparedFile`: write JSONL (or arbitrary non-AmpThread bytes); assert `PrepareTranscript` returns an error and `runner.threadID == ""`.
- Replace `TestPrepareTranscript_RunnerError`: pre-write prepared JSON, runner returns error, assert error propagates.
- Remove the JSONL-only `writeTestTranscript` helper (or repurpose for "unprepared" negative tests). Other tests that used `writeTestTranscript` for "expect unprepared error" can pass arbitrary JSONL bytes inline.

### Docs

`AGENT.md`

## Summary

Root cause: `amp` is a Bun-compiled native binary. When invoked from inside an Amp plugin (which runs on Bun), the plugin's child-process environment leaks `BUN_BE_BUN=1` (and friends) through `entire` → `entire-agent-amp` → `amp`. With those vars set, a Bun-compiled binary re-enters Bun's script-runner mode and reads `argv[1]` ("threads") as a script name — producing `error: Script not found "threads"`.

Fix (`internal/amp/command_runner.go`):
- New `ampEnv()` returns `os.Environ()` minus Bun bootstrap variables: `BUN_BE_BUN`, `BUN_INTERNAL_IPC_FD`, `BUN_INSPECT`, `BUN_INSPECT_NOTIFY`, `BUN_INSPECT_CONNECT_TO`, and anything matching `BUN_DEBUG_*`. User-meaningful vars like `BUN_INSTALL` are preserved.
- `DefaultCommandRunner.ExportThread` now passes `append(ampEnv(), "PLUGINS=all")` as the env for the `amp` subprocess.
- New unit tests `TestAmpEnvStripsBunVars` and `TestIsBunEnvVar` lock in the behavior.
